blocks.content: Distractor options are meticulously designed to match common calculation errors made under exam pressure.

rows: One clear correct answer and three distinct distractors
Includes answers derived from typical student miscalculations
Direct and standard phrasing with standard terminology
Employs subtle qualifiers, double negatives, or terms like 'EXCEPT'
Acts as a time-sink designed to disrupt pacing

items: Always re-check the required unit of measurement (e.g., km/h vs m/s) before locking your final answer.
Option (A) is intentionally placed as a surface-level trap for candidates who stop solving prematurely.
Beware of double negatives and hidden conditional words in UPSC and SSC statement-type questions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Distractor options frequently reflect the exact output of common formula or calculation mistakes.
Absolute qualifier words such as 'Always', 'Never', and 'Only' often signal incorrect statement choices.
Keywords like 'NOT', 'EXCEPT', and 'INCORRECT' are critical traps easily missed during rushed reading.
Spending excessive time on complex questions early creates fatigue and increases error rates later.
